Paper Title: DurianEdge-YOLO: A Lightweight Real-Time Durian Fruit Detection Framework with Adaptive Attention, Structured Pruning, and Knowledge Distillation for Dual-Platform Edge Deployment
Relevant Excerpt:
1. YOLO-Based Object Detection in Precision Agriculture:
 The YOLO family has dominated the lightweight detection literature for agricultural applications since YOLOv5 established a strong parameter-efficiency frontier in 2020. Recent iterations have substantially improved the architecture. YOLOv8  introduced an anchor-free detection head and C2f bottleneck blocks, achieving improved mAP while reducing inference time.

2. Current State of the Art:
 Lightweight agricultural object detection: YOLOv8n remains the dominant baseline with approximately 3.2M parameters and 8.1 GFLOPs at 640×640 input resolution, achieving 80-95% mAP50 across various crop detection tasks . YOLO11n and YOLO12n have improved this tradeoff, with YOLO11n achieving 56.9% mAP50-95 on COCO at 2.6M parameters.

3. Model Compression for Edge Deployment:
 For object detection, FGD  proposes focal distillation of foreground features, while CWD  aligns channelwise distributions between teacher and student. Recent work by Yang et al.  demonstrates that feature-level KD applied at the neck output consistently outperforms logit-level KD for YOLO architectures.
Abstract: Precision agriculture increasingly demands real-time, on-device inference for crop monitoring and yield estimation, yet deploying deep learning models on severely resource-constrained edge platforms remains a fundamental challenge. This paper presents DurianEdge-YOLO, a novel lightweight object detection framework specifically designed for real-time durian fruit (Durio zibethinus) detection on embedded devices. Unlike existing approaches that rely solely on backbone replacement for model compression, our method integrates four synergistic innovations applied to a YOLOv8n baseline: (1) a Lightweight Adaptive Attention Module (LAAM) that dynamically recalibrates spatial and channel features through a dual-branch depthwise mechanism with minimal parameter overhead, (2) an Efficient Adaptive Feature Fusion Neck (EAFFN) that replaces standard PAN/FPN concatenation with learned scalar-weighted multi-scale integration, (3) a unified two-stage compression pipeline combining structured L1-norm channel pruning with feature-level knowledge distillation from a YOLOv8m teacher, and (4) mixed-precision quantization-aware training (QAT) calibrated specifically for INT8 deployment on TensorRT and ONNX Runtime. We introduce DurianFruitDet-2024, a comprehensive benchmark dataset comprising [XX,XXX] images collected across real orchard conditions in Thailand and Malaysia, covering diverse illumination periods (morning, noon, evening), weather states, occlusion levels, viewpoints, distances, and camera devices. Extensive experiments on NVIDIA Jetson Nano (4GB) and Raspberry Pi 3 Model B+ demonstrate that DurianEdge-YOLO achieves [XX.X]% mAP50 and [XX.X]% mAP50-95 while operating at [XX.X] FPS on Jetson Nano (TensorRT INT8) and [X.X] FPS on Raspberry Pi 3 (NCNN INT8), representing a [XX]% speedup over YOLOv8n with [X.X]% mAP50 loss and [XX]% reduction in model size. Ablation studies quantitatively validate the individual and combined contribution of each component. Our framework establishes a new state-of-the-art for durian detection on resource-constrained hardware and provides a replicable methodology for edge deployment of agricultural AI systems.

Paper Title: Automatic Classification and Segmentation of Teeth on 3D dental model Using Hierarchical Deep Learning Networks
Author Names:
Sukun Tian
Ning Dai
Bei Zhang
Fulai Yuan
Qing Yu
Xiaosheng Cheng
Relevant Excerpt:
1. C. NETWORK ARCHITECTURE:
 In recent years, deep CNNs have been developed in a deeper, more flexible and effective training direction.
Abstract: To solve the problem of low efficiency, the complexity of interactive operation and the high degree of manual intervention in existing methods, we propose a novel approach based on sparse voxel octree and 3D Convolution Neural Networks(CNNs) for segmenting and classifying tooth types on 3D dental models. Firstly, the tooth classification method capitalized on two-level hierarchical feature learning is proposed to solve the misclassification problem in highly similar tooth categories. Secondly, we exploit an improved three-level hierarchical segmentation method based on deep convolution features to conduct segmentation of teeth-gingiva and inter-teeth respectively, and the conditional random field model is used to refine the boundary of the gingival margin and the inter-teeth fusion region. The experimental results show that the classification accuracy in Level_1 network is 95.96%, the average classification accuracy in Level_2 network is 88.06%, and the accuracy of tooth segmentation is 89.81%. Compared with the existing state-of-the-art methods, the proposed method has higher accuracy and universality, and it has great application potential in computer-assisted orthodontic treatment diagnosis.
